EU and non-EU companies who are accredited entities for CBAM reasons by EU Member States National Accreditation Bodies (NABs) and would like to become Registered CBAM Accredited Verifiers, must have access to the CBAM Third Country Operator Portal to register and report information about their company and their accreditation scopes.

Therefore, the purpose of this document is to provide the access request steps that should be followed by EU or non-EU Companies to get access to the CBAM Third Country Operators portal (CBAM O3CI portal) and also how to apply in the portal towards the NCAs to become Registered CBAM Accredited Verifier.

After the access request is approved, the Accredited CBAM Verifier will be able to access the CBAM Third Country Operator Portal, where he should perform additional steps to apply and become a registered CBAM Accredited Verifier and review the monitoring approach, emissions calculations and supporting evidence. These steps are described on the CBAM Registry – User manual for the O3CI Portal, available on the CBAM Registry website.

The specific portal to be used by the Accredited Entities for the management of their registration requests is the CBAM Registry – O3CI Portal – available at the website address: https://cbam.ec.europa.eu/o3cinstallation.
Please, note that EU access is a first step, to request the technical user access. This step is a prerequisite to request access to the CBAM registry.

The second step is for your business request for registration as a Registered Verifier in the CBAM registry. This step will be managed by the National Competent Authority of the country of accreditation.
The target audience for this document includes:
This document is organised as follows:
Chapter 1 – Introduction: describes the scope and the objectives of the document;

Chapter 2 – Business Guidance on the CBAM processes: describes the general guidance on the legal acts governing the CBAM domain, as well as guidance on the main processes and how to add data about the companies.
Chapter 3 - Step-by-step guidance for gaining access to O3CI Portal as Accredited Verifier: defines the guidelines and step-by-step procedure for granting access to the CBAM Registry.

Chapter 4 – User Responsibilities and Security Requirements: presents the user responsibilities and security requirements when using the IT system related to the management of access requests for the CBAM portal.

Chapter 5 – Helpdesk and user access management support: presents the helpdesk contact points that the verifier from the third countries may use in order to get support on the access management requests.

Chapter 6 – Further Guidance on the use of the O3CI Portal to manage your registration: defines the guidelines on how to consult the user manual for the CBAM Accredited Verifiers portal in order to apply to become a registered CBAM Accredited Verifiers.

2. BUSINESS GUIDANCE ON THE CBAM PROCESSES

To ensure compliance with the CBAM Regulation, the Accredited Entities and Third Country Operators Portal (CBAM O3CI) section of the CBAM Registry has been established. This portal allows the verifiers:
To apply to the EU National Competent Authorities (NCAs) to become a Registered CBAM Accredited Verifier;
To start a collaboration request between the Registered Accredited Verifier and the Registered Operator of Third Country Installations;
To verify operator’s emissions report calculation and to issue the verification report, corresponding to yearly emissions for that installation.
Implementation in the CBAM Registry of the CBAM verification in third country installation was done based on the following legislative acts:
Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2546 - on the application of verification principles;
Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/2551 - on accreditation and verification;
Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2547 - on methods for the calculation of emissions embedded in goods.

Please note that Article 14(4) of the CBAM Regulation addresses confidentiality, specifying that the CBAM registry data under Article 10(2) shall remain confidential. However, names, addresses, and contact information of operators and the locations of installations in third countries may be made public. Operators have however the option to withhold their names, addresses, and contact information from public access.
2.2 REQUIRED DOCUMENTS TO BE SUBMITTED BY THE ACCREDITED VERIFIERS FOR THE ACCESS REQUEST

When submitting the request for access as an Accredited Entity (Accredited Verifier) to the CBAM - EU Access system to request access, please prepare and submit the following business types of documents:

Accreditation Certificate: Demonstrates that the accredited entity applied to be an accredited verifier and that the NAB provided it with this document and includes essential details (name, address, contact information, and tax ID or equivalent).

Company registration documentation: Demonstrates that the company that will be accredited as verifier provided the legally relevant documentation that identifies the company as a registered legal entity in the country of origin.
Identity document of the person acting on behalf of the accredited entity: Identity document of the representative, like national identity card or passport.

To send the 3 types of documents at once in the system, please merge the documents into one single pdf file and upload the pdf file in the request for access from the EU Access system (as detailed in chapter 3.3.7 - EU Access on-boarding – step 5 – last step, on page 25).

It is strongly recommended to upload supporting documents in English language. Supporting documents which are not in English language may result in delays in the accredited entity's access request processing.
2.3 GUIDANCE FOR KEY ACCREDITED ENTITY IDENTIFIERS

Accredited Entity Identifier – Accredited Entity ID/Corporate Registration Number (CRN): Accredited Entity Identifier represents the corporate registration number. This is a unique identifier assigned to a business entity upon its official registration with a national or regional business registry. This number serves as proof of a company's legal existence and is used for identification and record-keeping purposes by government agencies, financial institutions, and regulatory authorities. The format of this identifier varies by country, often consisting of a series of numbers, letters, or a combination that uniquely identifies the business. The company identifier should start with the 2-letter country code for the country where the company is registered. The maximum length of this identifier is 25 characters.

Please note that the Accredited Entities located in a country of the European Union may declare either their Tax identification number or their Corporate Registration number at the Registry of Commerce in the Member State in this field.
BEABCD12345 (BE for the 2-letter country-code for Belgium, followed by some letters and numbers)

3. STEP-BY-STEP GUIDANCE FOR GAINING ACCESS TO O3CI PORTAL AS ACCREDITED VERIFIER
With regards to O3CI Portal users, there are four types of actors that can gain access to the O3CI Portal. Table 5 presents the four types of actors:
This refers to the legal entity. It can be the CEO/legal representative for the operator who applies for access to the O3CI portal.
This refers to a natural person (employee) who receives a delegation by the TCO to access the O3CI portal.
This refers to the legal entity. Accredited verifier is an independent third-party auditor, accredited by a NABs (National Accreditation Bodies from the EU).
This refers to a natural person (employee) who receives a delegation by the ACEO to access the O3CI portal. Permissions are the same as for the main actor ACEO.
The Accredited Entity is the legal entity that initially requests access to the O3CI portal. A high-level view of this process is depicted below:
Figure 2: O3CI types of actors, roles and relationship

Accredited Entity can gain access to the CBAM Definitive Registry and then apply to become Regitered Verifier to the National Competent Authority (NCA) of the country where they have been accredited by a National Accreditation Body (NAB).

Once the Accredited Verifier is a Registered verifier, then they may start a collaboration request – through the CBAM Registry – with the Operators of Third Country Installations. Aim of this collaboration is for the Operators to communicate to the Accredited Verifier the emissions report and for the Verifier to produce the Verification Report in the CBAM Registry.

Once the Verification Report is produced, then the Operator of Third Country Installation may share the verified emissions information through the CBAM Registry with the importer in the EU who is authorised CBAM declarant.

As a final step, the EU Authorised CBAM declarant, in the CBAM Registry – Declaration Lifecycle Management module – will lodge their yearly CBAM Declaration using verified actual emissions shared by the Operator from the Verification Report.
A pre-requisite for ACEO to request access to the O3CI Portal is the creation of an EU Login account.

EU Login is the entry gate to sign in to different European Commission services and/or other systems. EU Login verifies your identity and allows recovering your personal settings, history and access rights in a secure way.
For guidelines on how to create an EU Login account, please refer to the relevant EU Login frequently-asked-questions (FAQs).

Please note that to authenticate in EU Login a 2-factor authentication is required, so this needs to be appropriately setup. Please consult the EU Login tutorial in order to select the preferred authentication method among the options below:
Depending on the country, the availability of authentication methods may vary.
For the CBAM O3CI Portal, the recommended 2-factor authentication methods are any of the following:
EU Login Mobile App PIN Code;
EU Login Mobile App QR Code;

Please note that in some countries the Google or Apple stores/services might not be available, thus the EU Login Mobile App is not available. In these cases, to authenticate you need to register your Security Key or Trusted Platform. The only requirement for the security key is to be FIDO2 certified (e.g. Yubikey).
You will be able to register a Security Key/Trusted Platform following the EU Login tutorial on this matter, which also includes a video tutorial with the necessary steps.

3.3.8 Validation error messages that could appear when filling-in request for technical access

While completing the request for technical access, some validation error messages may appear in the case that what you fill-in is not correct or not accurate according to the defined validation rule for the respective field.
In this chapter, you are shown how a validation error message appears on your screen and what does every message mean in practical terms.
Figure 12: EU Access Onboarding Wizard – Step 5 - Review and Submission – Error messages
When the final step of the onboarding wizard is loaded, if the company data has been entered correctly, no error messages will be displayed at the top of the screen.

If at least one of the company details was not provided in the expected format in the previous steps, one or more error messages will appear in red at the top of the screen, highlighting the fields that failed validation.
The following error(s) may occur and could be shown once or multiple times:
VAL748 The attribute [Company Identifier] has invalid value [xxxxx], please check the onboarding manual for more details.

This error occurs when the value entered in the "Company Identifier" attribute (in step 4 of the wizard) violates one or more of the rules outlined in Table 9. If the error appears multiple times, it indicates that at least two rules have been violated.

Once the access request was created, an administrator at the European Commission will review it, and you will be notified of its approval or rejection via email. Please be aware that this process may take several days after submission. The following scenarios are possible:

3.4 STEP-BY-STEP GUIDANCE FOR SUBMITTING A REGISTRATION REQUEST IN O3CI PORTAL

Once the user logs in to the Operators of Third Countries Installations Portal as an accredited entity, the Homepage is displayed. The homepage provides access to several sections through two navigation methods: widgets and a left sidebar menu. Both allow users to jump directly to the corresponding forms.

To complete the registration process as an Accredited Verifier after the access is granted in the Operators of Third Countries Installations Portal, please submit a registration request following the steps described below.

For more in-depth details on the functioning of the Operators of Third Country Installations Portal, please check the CBAM Registry website – User Manual for the Accredited Verifiers and Operators of Third Country Installations portal).
When user logs in to the CBAM Registry – O3CI portal for the first time the “Homepage” is displayed as the default page. The user selects the “Accredited Entity Information” option.
Figure 16: O3CI Verifier registration request – Step 1
On the top of the Accredited Entity Information page the State contains the value “New” and on the right hand side the option “Start Registration Request” is displayed.
Figure 17: O3CI Verifier registration request – Step 2
Additionally, the View History button is displayed on the left of Start registration Request button, that keeps records of the actions taken during the registration of the accredited entity.

The accredited entity user having the Admin user permissions clicks on the “Start Registration Request” button. User can start entering the Accredited Entity information. “The Start Registration Request” button is hidden and, in its place, the following buttons are displayed: “Close and Resume Later”, “Delete Request”, “Submit Request”. The “View History” button remains available.
Figure 18: O3CI Verifier registration request – Step 3

The user can now start entering information regarding the accredited entity company details. As also can be seen from the above screenshot, the user can close and resume later from the respective “Close and Resume later” button.
The “Delete Request” and “Submit Request” buttons are still disabled and will be enabled once information is starting to be entered and the request starts to be forming by entering that information.
The type of request contains the value “Registration Request”.
User enters the details of the company, Address, Contact details in the “Accredited entity company details” tab.

When user fills in all the mandatory fields in the “Accredited entity company details” tab, the button “Save” at the bottom of the page is still deactivated. This happens because there is still information to be filled in the Accreditation details tab.
Figure 19: O3CI Verifier registration request – Step 4
After all the necessary information has been completed in the “Accredited entity company details” tab, the user can proceed with the information in the Accreditation details tab.
Once all the necessary information has been completed, then the save button becomes enabled, thus letting the user save the updates made so far.
Figure 20: O3CI Verifier registration request – Step 5

Although both tabs (Accredited entity company details and Accreditation details tabs) have been filled in with information, still the “Accreditation supporting documents” tab is disabled and most importantly the “Submit request” button is disabled.

To proceed with the submission of the request* the “Accreditation supporting documents” tab is imperative to be filled-in as well. To proceed with the “Accreditation supporting documents” tab first the user needs to press the save button that is now enabled.

Note (*): Only Admin users can submit a registration request. Simple user can only fill-in the details across the three tabs: “Accredited entity company details”, “Accreditation details”, “Accreditation supporting documents” and save the request.
Now it’s time for the Admin User to submit the registration request, as all the information has been entered.
Once the Admin User logs in to the application, the available actions are the “View History” and “Continue Registration Request”.
After admin user clicks on the “Continue Registration Request” button the actions available to the user are “View History”, ”Close and Resume Later”, ”Delete Request” and ”Submit request”.

Once the Accredited Entity Company Details, Accreditation Details tabs requested information has been filled-in and Accreditation supporting documents have been uploaded, an information text will be displayed in the top right corner of the application indicating the user that the upload has been completed successfully or unsuccessfully respectively.
For the uploaded document the user has the option to either edit, download or delete the document.
Now that all the necessary information has been provided from the user, the “Submit request” button is enabled, thus allowing the user to submit the registration request.
Figure 23: O3CI Verifier registration request – Step 7
User now clicks the “Submit Request” button, a submit request pop up notification message is displayed informing the user about the request that is going to be sent.
Figure 24: Verification message displayed upon user attempt to submit request

User at this point has the option to click “Cancel” button and cancel the submission procedure. Data entered so far is saved and user will be able to proceed again to the submission of the request at another moment in time.

To ensure the security of the O3CI Portal, all users, including Accredited Entity (ACEO) and their delegated employees (ACEEMPL), must adhere to specific responsibilities and security requirements. The European Commission invests significant time and resources in implementing effective controls to mitigate risks and vulnerabilities. However, the security of information also relies on the care exercised by users in their day-to-day roles.

O3CI Administrator has specific tasks and responsibilities within the O3CI Portal. These responsibilities include managing their accounts, installations, and user delegations efficiently. The key tasks and responsibilities of O3CI Administrator are as follows:

Request for Registration: Accredited Entities can submit a request for registration to the National Competent Authority of the country where the National Accreditation Body has accredited the respective verifier. Verifier will send details of their company, accreditation scope and accreditation certificate, making this information available to the National Competent Authorities.
Delegation of Users: Accredited Entity Administrator can delegate access rights to the CBAM Registry - O3CI Portal for their employees without requiring additional approvals.
The Accredited Entity Administrator is obliged to provide true and valid information in their access requests and submissions.

By fulfilling these tasks and responsibilities, Accredited Entity Administrator gains access to the O3CI Portal where they submit information to the National Competent Authorities. Only the National Competent Authorities are solely responsible for the verification of information submitted by the Accredited Verifiers during the Registration process.
To prioritise information security and ensure compliance with regulatory standards, users must adhere to the following security requirements:
Data protection rules of GDPR [R01] and IDPR [R02] are applicable to the O3CI Portal;
Under the O3CI Portal regulation [R03], all information in O3CI Portal shall be covered by the obligation of professional secrecy (art 13 § 1[2]);

All information acquired by the competent Authority or the Commission in the course of performing their duties which is by its nature confidential, or which is provided on a confidential basis shall be covered by the obligation of professional secrecy. Such information shall not be disclosed by the competent Authority or the Commission without the express prior permission of the person or Authority that provided it or by virtue of Union or national law.
Users must follow the principles of least privilege, need to know, need to use.
In addition to the password requirements[3] enforced by EU Login, every user plays a vital role in safeguarding their access. To further enhance information security, each user must:
As set out in the EU Login Tutorial
Utilize a strong password and regularly update it (e.g., every 90 days);
Never share their password with anyone or allow others to use their account;
Avoid writing down or storing passwords electronically, such as in files or emails;
Refrain from using the same password for personal or other business-related accounts;
Avoid displaying any information containing access credentials, such as login names and passwords;
Notify the appropriate authorities of any changes in their role or access requirements;
Notify if the account has been leaked or compromised and immediately change the password.
Finally, the use of a Password Manager application is strongly recommended.

Compliance with CBAM security requirements described in this document (4.2 User Security Requirements and Responsibilities) is mandatory for all individuals accessing the O3CI Portal. Any non-compliance or violation of these requirements shall be reported, investigated, and appropriate actions shall be taken. Regular audits and reviews shall be conducted to assess adherence to this document and the effectiveness of user access controls internally by O3CIs.

5. HELPDESK AND USER ACCESS MANAGEMENT SUPPORT
Verifiers may encounter access management issues or difficulties attempting to access the CBAM O3CI Portal.
In such cases, it is important to ensure an efficient resolution by accurately categorizing and communicating the nature of the user access management issues or requests.
In the event of any issues, Accredited Entities should send an email to the address: customs-support@itsmtaxud.europa.eu for support.
The official language of communication when reaching out to the email address is English.
The working hours of the support desk is 07:00 – 21:00 CET/Europe-Belgium time-zone, Monday to Friday.
The following information should be included in the email with to the helpdesk request to facilitate effective troubleshooting:
URL in Use: The specific URL where the issue is occurring;
Screenshot of the Error: An attachment of a screenshot reflecting the error message displayed;
Timestamp of the Error: The date and time when the issue occurred.
6. FURTHER GUIDANCE ON THE USE OF THE O3CI PORTAL TO MANAGE YOUR REGISTRATION AS ACCREDITED VERIFIER

Once the Accredited Entity has requested access to the CBAM Third Country Operators portal (CBAM O3CI Portal) and the access request has been approved by the European Commission, as presented in the previous chapters, the next step is to access the CBAM O3CI Portal.
The CBAM O3CI Portal is available at the address https://cbam.ec.europa.eu/o3cinstallation.
To be further guided on how to use the portal, please consult the CBAM Registry – User manual for the O3CI Portal, available on the CBAM Registry website.
